summary: SECOND REVIEW OF THIS SCOPE — tools/governor/reorient.mjs ONLY, the session-start orientation hook. The first review returned request_changes with one HIGH / ACTIVE / BLOCKS_CURRENT_MERGE finding. It was REAL, I confirmed it by execution rather than by reading, and it is repaired in this diff. JUDGE THE REPAIR, not my account of it. CONTEXT. BUILD-018 built a session governor that enforced 0 of its 4 intended rules and is being torn down surgically rather than reverted, because a blind revert would take genuinely useful components with it. reorient.mjs SURVIVES, decoupled. It is the hook that runs at session start and tells the operator where the session actually is — repository, worktree, branch, HEAD — plus which loose deliverables are open and what the continuity brief points at. WHAT THIS DIFF DOES. reorient.mjs is decoupled from the two deleted modules it depended on, falling from 1265 lines to 347 before the repair. It previously walked the whole estate looking for Deliverables/*/programme-state.json, collapsed multiple checkouts, and assessed the freshness of banked programme commits; all of that machinery is deleted along with programme-state.mjs and rotate-session.mjs. What remains is the three behaviours worth keeping: the sweep of loose Deliverables/*.md plans, the passthrough of the Honcho continuity brief, and repository/worktree/branch/HEAD verification by real git calls. Exactly one four-line helper, normaliseSeparators, was inlined from the deleted rotate-session.mjs. Its sibling isBankingCommit was deliberately NOT inlined, because its only consumer was the deleted freshness assessment — inlining it would have re-grown a corpse, and the comment at line 53 records that reasoning rather than leaving it to be rediscovered. WHY THE DECOUPLING MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. The orientation hook is the first thing that speaks in every session, and it is the component that tells the operator whether the state he is being shown was measured or assumed. A decoupling that quietly dropped one of the three behaviours would degrade every future session's opening, silently, in a way that reads exactly like a session with nothing to report. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED, stated so a limit is never mistaken for coverage. (1) Nothing in this diff has run in CI; all test counts come from one Windows machine. (2) The tests for this module live in tools/governor/reorient.test.mjs, which CANNOT be staged into a review packet untruncated — its diff exceeds the 60,000-byte cap and the repair made it LARGER, not smaller — so the criteria about test existence and mutation-testing are NOT gated by this packet and are not offered as reviewed. That limit is disclosed here and recorded in the phase record; it is not implied. (3) reorient.test.mjs remains excluded from the CI workflow. (4) Two of the ten surviving modules, continuity.mjs and continuity-derive.mjs, have NO TEST FILES AT ALL — zero coverage, not merely unproven wiring. (5) worktree-guard.mjs survives as a file but is INERT: it reads Deliverables/*/programme-state.json off disk itself, so with no programme present it returns defer for every guarded tool. That is reported deliberately and NOT repaired, because building a replacement guard is precisely the regrowth this reset exists to cut. (6) The case-recovery behaviour of the repair is proven on win32 only. All evidence behind this claim is builder self-test plus my own independent re-run of every number and every probe. It is NOT independent review, which is what you are being asked for.
brief_excerpt:
Judge this diff against these acceptance criteria and ONLY these. C1, C2 and C3 were written BEFORE the diff existed, derived from the work order rather than from the code, so they cannot be back-fitted to whatever was built.

SCOPE — read this first, so a scope artefact is never mistaken for a defect. This packet contains tools/governor/reorient.mjs ONLY. (1) Rows concerning any other file are OUT OF SCOPE: mark them not_applicable, never blocked, and do not let the absence of other files reduce your confidence in the rows below. (2) The tests for this module are in tools/governor/reorient.test.mjs, a file that cannot be staged untruncated and is therefore NOT part of this packet — do not report tests as missing from this one, and do not infer from their absence that they do not exist. (3) tools/governor/footer.mjs and tools/governor/sampler.mjs are reviewed under their own separate claims.

C1. reorient.mjs no longer imports programme-state.mjs or rotate-session.mjs. Both modules are deleted in this teardown, so a surviving import would not merely be untidy — it would be a hard runtime failure at session start.

C2. reorient.mjs still performs all THREE preserved behaviours, and this is the row that matters most, because a decoupling that silently drops one degrades the opening of every future session in a way indistinguishable from a session with nothing to report:
  (a) the sweep of loose Deliverables/*.md plans;
  (b) the Honcho continuity brief passthrough;
  (c) repository / worktree / branch / HEAD verification by real git calls, not by assumption.
Verify each is genuinely reachable in the shipped code path — that is, wired into the hook's output rather than merely present as an exported function nothing calls. An orphaned export that no path reaches satisfies a grep and fails the criterion.

C3. Exactly ONE helper, normaliseSeparators, was inlined from the deleted rotate-session.mjs. isBankingCommit was NOT inlined, deliberately, because its only consumer was the deleted assessBankedFreshness. Confirm no other symbol was quietly carried across from either deleted module, and that no dead helper arrived with no caller.

PRIOR FINDING AND ITS REPAIR — HAND-CARRIED BY ME, and disclosed because undisclosed curation is worse than none. There is NO automated route by which prior review findings reach you: this tool takes only a local claim file that I author. The following is therefore a HUMAN TRANSCRIPTION, and my account of what was fixed is an assertion for you to TEST, not a fact to accept.

PRIOR F1 (HIGH, ACTIVE, BLOCKS_CURRENT_MERGE): worktreePath was the caller's own argument handed straight back, unmeasured, then printed beneath the heading 'executed, not assumed' and above the closing line 'These are facts'. Every other field in that object came from executing git. Confirmed by execution: a path not present on disk rendered verbatim in that block. A THIRD instance of the same class was then found by the builder which NEITHER the reviewer NOR I had spotted — the incoming value is never type-checked and normaliseSeparators passes a non-string through unchanged, so a cwd of 7 rendered as the line 'cwd : 7' under the same heading. A related defect in the same block collapsed 'git could not run at all' and 'this branch genuinely has no upstream' into a single confident sentence claiming nothing is pushed.

WHAT WAS DONE: gitFacts now additionally returns resolvedPath, from fs.realpathSync.native inside the existing soft() guard — a genuine measurement, chosen over a mere existence check because it also recovers the TRUE ON-DISK CASING and so removes the underlying disagreement between the reported cwd and the git-measured repo root. It also returns gitReadable, a rev-parse --git-dir probe recording whether git answered at all, deliberately NON-nullable and failing closed. The cwd line now renders three visibly distinct outcomes: the measured path; '(UNVERIFIED — no path was supplied)'; and '(UNVERIFIED — host reported X; no such directory on disk)'. The upstream line asserts that nothing is pushed ONLY when gitReadable is true. The route deliberately MEASURES the value rather than relabelling or deleting the field, on the reasoning that the cwd-versus-repo-root comparison is how a wrong-location session becomes visible to a human, so deleting the field would trade a lie for a blind spot.

Y1. ATTACK THE REPAIR DIRECTLY. Can any input still reach that block and render a value the module did not establish? Consider a path that exists but is not a directory; a symlink or junction; a UNC path; a path that exists but is unreadable; the empty string; a boolean, array or object supplied as cwd; and a path that resolves successfully but on which git nonetheless partially fails. Name concrete inputs rather than describing categories.
Y2. Is gitReadable itself trustworthy? Can it report true where git did not actually answer, or false where it did? It is now the sole gate on a POSITIVE claim about the remote, so a wrong value there re-creates the original defect in the opposite direction, which is harder to notice.
Y3. Does the three-way cwd rendering ever LOSE information a reader needs, or render an unestablished value in a form a reader could mistake for an established one? The whole purpose of the repair is that the difference is visible to a human, not merely present in the data.

Z1. The hook must never THROW. reorient.mjs runs at session start; if it throws, the operator's first contact with the session is a crash or, worse, silence. Verify that a missing Deliverables directory, an unreadable file, an absent continuity brief, and a git call that fails or returns nothing each degrade to a reported absence rather than an exception. The repair added filesystem and git calls, so this row is materially more exposed than it was at the first review.

Z2. The hook must never report a state it did not MEASURE. This is the module's entire reason for existing: it is the component that distinguishes verified location from assumed location. Find any path where repository, worktree, branch, HEAD or upstream could be rendered as fact from a default, a stale value, or a silently swallowed git failure. A confidently-rendered wrong branch is strictly worse than no branch at all, because the operator acts on it.

ADVERSARIAL ROWS — answer these even if every row above passes.
W1. Can the deliverables sweep miss a file it should report, or report one it should not? Consider unreadable entries, symlinks, deeply nested paths, case sensitivity on a case-insensitive filesystem, and files whose frontmatter is malformed.
W2. Can any of the three preserved behaviours fail SILENTLY — producing an empty or absent section that looks identical to a genuine 'nothing to report'? Name the concrete input.
W3. normaliseSeparators was inlined from deleted code. Does its inlined form behave identically to every use site that depends on it, including UNC paths, mixed separators, and trailing separators?
W4. Is there any remaining coupling to programme-state — by filename, by convention, by directory layout, or by an assumption about what exists on disk — that a grep for imports would not catch?

OUT OF SCOPE — do not report these as defects: which modules the operator chose to keep or delete (a product decision, not a code question); prose, naming or comment-style preference; the absence of tests from THIS packet (see scope note 2); the lack of CI execution, the zero coverage of continuity.mjs and continuity-derive.mjs, and the inert worktree-guard.mjs, all of which are disclosed in the summary above and already recorded; and the absence of malicious-handler hardening, since this estate's defect bar is correctness, accidental leak, availability and audit for a first-party personal system, not a hostile-input service.
